$a = 5ms^{- 2}$

questions.solution:

$Tcos\theta = mg$

$⇒ T = \dfrac{mg}{\cos 30 °} ⇒ T = \dfrac{\sqrt{3} \times 10}{\dfrac{3}{2}}$

questions.q: A uniform metal chain of mass $m$~and length $L$~passes over a massless and frictionless pulley. It is released from rest with a part of its length $l$~is hanging on one side and rest of its length $L - l$ is hanging on the other side of the pulley. At a certain point of time, when $l = \dfrac{L}{x}$, the acceleration of the chain is $\dfrac{g}{2}$. The value of $x$ is _____.
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
According to the information given in the question, the part of the chain that envelopes the pulley is very small. Therefore, the acceleration of the chain can be written as,

$a = \left({m}_{2} - {m}_{1}\right)\left({m}_{2} + {m}_{1}\right)g$

Since~$a = \dfrac{g}{2}$

$\dfrac{g}{2} = \left({m}_{2} - {m}_{1}\right)\left({m}_{2} + {m}_{1}\right)g ⇒ \dfrac{g}{2} = \dfrac{\left(L - l\right) - l}{L}g ⇒ l = \dfrac{L}{4} = \dfrac{L}{x}$

$⇒ x = 4$

The coefficient of kinetic friction between the object and the surface of inclined plane is :

questions.solution: Case-1 : No friction $\begin{aligned} & \mathrm{a}=\mathrm{g} \sin \theta \\ & \ell=\frac{1}{2}(\mathrm{~g} \sin \theta) \mathrm{t}_1^2 \\ & \mathrm{t}_1=\sqrt{\frac{2 \ell}{\mathrm{g} \sin \theta}} \end{aligned}$ Case-2 : With friction $\begin{aligned} & \mathrm{a}=\mathrm{g} \sin \theta-\mu \mathrm{g} \cos \theta \\ & \ell=\frac{1}{2}(\mathrm{~g} \sin \theta-\mu \mathrm{g} \cos \theta) \mathrm{t}_2^2 \\ & \sqrt{\frac{2 \ell}{\mathrm{g} \sin \theta-\mu g \cos \theta}}=\mathrm{n} \sqrt{\frac{2 \ell}{\mathrm{g} \sin \theta}} \\ & \mu=1-\frac{1}{\mathrm{n}^2} \end{aligned}$

questions.q: A block of mass $m$ slides down the plane inclined at angle $30 °$ with an acceleration $\dfrac{g}{4}$ . The value of coefficient of kinetic friction will be :
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
Applying Newton's second law along the direction perpendicular to inlined plane:

$N - mgcos{30}^{∘} = 0$~(As $\theta = 30 °$)

(since the acceleration of block in the direction perpendicular to the inclined plane is $0$)

$∴ N = mgcos{30}^{∘}$~ ~.....(1)

Let $\mu$~be the coefficient of kinetic friction between the block and the inclined plane. Applying Newton's second law along inclined plane:

$mgsin{30}^{∘} - \muN = ma = m\dfrac{g}{4}$~ ~ ....(2)

(since the acceleration along the inclined plane, $a = \dfrac{g}{4}$)

$∴ mgsin{30}^{∘} - \mu mgcos{30}^{∘} = m\dfrac{g}{4}$~ ~(from equation 1 and 2)

$⇒ \dfrac{mg}{2} - \dfrac{3}{2}\mumg = m\dfrac{g}{4}$

$⇒\mu = \dfrac{1}{2\sqrt{3}}$

$a = \lleft(4\sqrt{3} -1)$~$ms^{- 1}$

Applying Newton's second law for second block (along the direction parallel to the incline on which it is placed)

$T - 5 = 1 \timesa$

$⇒ T = 5 + 4\sqrt{3} -1$

$= 4\left(\sqrt{3} +1\right)N$

questions.q:
The initial mass of a rocket is $1000$ kg. Calculate at what rate the fuel should be burnt so that the rocket is given an acceleration of,~$20{ms}^{- 2}$. The gases come out at a relative speed of $500\mathrm\mathrm\mathrm\mathrm\mathrm\mathrm\mathrm\mathrm\mathrm\mathrm\mathrm\mathrm{ms}^{-1}$, with respect to the rocket:

\left[\text{Use}g = 10ms^{- 2}\right]$

$
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
Here we are applying the equation,& ${F}_{r} - mg = ma$

From Newton's second law,~${F}_{r} = \dfrac{dm}{dt}{v}_{r}⇒ \dfrac{dm}{dt}{v}_{r} = mg + ma$

Put the given values in the above equations,~

$⇒ \dfrac{dm}{dt}500 = 1000 ( 10 + 20 )⇒ \dfrac{dm}{dt} = 60kgs^{- 1}$.

questions.q: A block of mass $10$ kg starts sliding on a surface with an initial velocity of $9 . 8\mathrm\mathrm\mathrm\mathrm\mathrm\mathrm\mathrm\mathrm\mathrm\mathrm\mathrm\mathrm{ms}^{-1}$. The coefficient of friction between the surface and block is $0 . 5$. The distance covered by the block before coming to rest is :[use~$g = 9 . 8{ms}^{- 2}$]
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
Given initial velocity& $u = 9 . 8ms^{- 1}$.

Acceleration~$a = \mug = 0 . 5 \times 9 . 8 = 4 . 9ms^{- 2}$

Using,~$v^{2} = u^{2} + 2as$, here, final velocity~$v = 0$.

So,~$0 = \left(9 . 8\right)2 + 2\left(4 . 9\right)s ⇒ s = 9 . 8m$

questions.q: A block of mass $5$ kg~is placed at rest on a table of rough surface. Now, if a force of $30N$~is applied in the direction parallel to surface of the table, the block slides through a distance of $50m$ in an interval of time $10s$. Coefficient of kinetic friction is (given, $g = 10ms^{– 2}$ ):
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
Forces acting on block is shown below

From the second equation of motion,

$s = \dfrac{1}{2}at^{2} ⇒ 50 = \dfrac{1}{2}a \times {10}^{2} ⇒ a = 1ms^{- 2}$

Applying Newton's second law in vertical direction,

$R - mg = 0 ⇒ R = mg$

(where~$R$~is the magnitude of normal reaction on the block due to the surface)

If $\mu$~is the coefficient of kinetic friction between the block and the surface, applying Newton's second law in horizontal direction,

$30 - \muR = ma ⇒ 30 - \mumg = ma ⇒ 30 - 50\mu = 5 ⇒ \mu = \dfrac{1}{2} = 0 . 5$

questions.q: A balloon has mass of $10g$ in air. The air escapes from the balloon at a uniform rate with velocity $4 . 5cms^{- 1}$. If the balloon shrinks in $5s$ completely. Then, the average force acting on that balloon will be (in dyne).
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
Given that the mass of the air& $m = 10g$~and it escapes in time~$t = 5s$~with velocity~$v = 4 . 5cms^{- 1}$.

The average force on the balloon can be given as,

$F = v\dfrac{d m}{d t}$

$⇒ F = 4 . 5 \times \dfrac{10}{5} = 9dyne$

questions.q: A body of mass $500g$ moves along $x$-axis such that it's velocity varies with displacement $x$ according to the relation $v = 10\sqrt{x}ms^{- 1}$ the force acting on the body is:
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
It is given that&

& $v = 10\sqrt{x}ms^{- 1}$

Force is defined by~$F = m\dfrac{dv}{dt} . . . ( i )$

Multiplying and dividing equation (i) by~$dx$

$F = m\dfrac{dv}{dt}\dfrac{dx}{dx} ⇒ F = m\dfrac{dx}{dt}\dfrac{dv}{dx} = mv\dfrac{dv}{dx} . . . ( ii )$

Finding the values of the terms in equation (ii)
$\dfrac{dv}{dx} = \dfrac{10}{2\sqrt{x}} = \dfrac{5}{x}$
$v\dfrac{dv}{dx} = a = 10\sqrt{x} \times \dfrac{5}{x} = 50ms^{- 2}$

Hence, the force is~
$F = \dfrac{1}{2} \times 50 = 25N$.

questions.q: A body of mass $10$ kg is moving with an initial speed of $20ms^{- 1}$. The body stops after $5s$ due to friction between body and the floor. The value of the coefficient of friction is: (Take acceleration due to gravity $g = 10ms^{- 2}$)
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
Friction force wil act opposite to the motion of the body.

$F = \muN = \mumg$

$⇒ a = - \mug \left(\text{-ve sign for direction relative to the motion of body}\right)

Now, applying equation of motion, we get

$v = u + at$

$⇒ 0 = 20 + \left(- \mu \times$10\right)$\times$5$

$⇒ 50\mu = 20$

~$⇒ \mu = 0 . 4

$

questions.q: A body of mass $4$ kg experiences two forces $\overset{→}{F}1 = 5\overset{^}{i} + 8\overset{^}{j} + 7\overset{^}{k}$ and $\overset{→}{F}2 = 3\overset{^}{i} - 4\overset{^}{j} - 3\overset{^}{k .}$ The acceleration acting on the body is:

questions.solution:
Net force $\overset{→}{F} = \overset{→}{F}1 + \overset{→}{F}2 = 8\overset{^}{i} + 4\overset{^}{j} + 4\overset{^}{k}$

Therefore, required acceleration $\overset{→}{a} = \overset{→}{F}m = 2\overset{^}{i} + \overset{^}{j} + \overset{^}{k}$

questions.q: A uniform chain of $6m$ length is placed on a table such that a part of its length is hanging over the edge of the table. The system is at rest. The co-efficient of static friction between the chain and the surface of the table is $0 . 5$, the maximum length of the chain hanging from the table is _____~$m$.
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
Let,& $\lambda =$mass per unit length of the chain and length of mass hanging through the table is~$x$.

Normal force applied by the table on the chain will be,~$N = \left(l - x\right)\lambdag$.

Tension developed in the chain will balance the gravitational force acting in the downward direction,~$T = \lambdaxg$.

Maximum limiting force possible for the part of the table,~${f}_\max = \muN = \mu\left(l - x\right)\lambdag$

For equilibrium,

${f}_\max = T$,

$⇒ \mu\left(l - x\right)\lambdag = \lambdaxg ⇒ \dfrac{1}{2} \times \left(6 - x\right) = x ⇒ x = 2m$

questions.q: An inclined plane is bent in such a way that the vertical cross-section is given by $y = \dfrac{x2}{4}$ where $y$ is in vertical and $x$ in horizontal direction. If the upper surface of this curved plane is rough with coefficient of friction $\mu = 0 . 5,$ the maximum height in $cm$ at which a stationary block will not slip downward is________cm .
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
At maximum ht. block will experience maximum friction force. Therefore if at this height slope of the tangent is $tan\theta,$~then $\theta =$Angle of repose

$∴ tan\theta = \dfrac{dy}{dx} = \dfrac{2x}{4} = \dfrac{x}{2} = 0 . 5$

questions.q: When a body slides down from rest along a smooth inclined plane making an angle of $30 °$ with the horizontal, it takes time $T .$~When the same body slides down from the rest along a rough inclined plane making the same angle and through the same distance, it takes time $\alphaT,$~where $\alpha$ is a constant greater than $1 .$ The co-efficient of friction between the body and the rough plane is $\dfrac{1}{x} \left(\dfrac{{α}^{2} - 1}{\alpha2}\right) where $x = __________ .
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
On smooth incline,

$a = gsin30 °$

by $S = ut + \dfrac{1}{2}at^{2}$

$S = \dfrac{1}{2}\dfrac{g}{2}T^{2} = \dfrac{g}{4}T^{2} . . . ( i )$

On rough incline

$a = gsin30 ° - \mu gcos30 °$

by $S = ut + \dfrac{1}{2}at^{2}$

$S = \dfrac{1}{4}g ( 1 - \sqrt{3}\mu ) ( \alphaT{)}^{2} . . . ( ii )$

By $( i )$ and $( ii )$

$\dfrac{1}{4}gT^{2} = \dfrac{1}{4}g ( 1 - \sqrt{3}\mu ) {α}^{2}T^{2}$

$⇒ 1 - \sqrt{3}\mu = \dfrac{1}{\alpha2} ⇒ \mu = \left(\dfrac{{α}^{2} - 1}{\alpha2}\right)\dfrac{1}{3}$

$⇒ x = 3 . 00$
